package_info.package_name: Lumma Stealer (delivered via MediaFire spam campaign)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as executable via MediaFire, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware delivered as a standalone binary, not versioned via package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The distributed executable is identified as Lumma Stealer, a well-known infostealer malware. It is delivered through unsolicited spam comments on GitHub issues, luring users to download and execute a malicious file. Upon execution, the malware compromises the victim's system by stealing browser-stored credentials, cookies, and environment variables, exfiltrating this data to a remote command-and-control (C2) server, and hijacking the user's GitHub account to propagate itself further through automated spam.

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (after clicking spam link and executing downloaded file)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious executable downloaded from MediaFire (filename varies, e.g., .exe or .zip archive)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [Binary executable: Lumma Stealer payload, not shown as source code]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the user manually executes the downloaded file, the binary enumerates browser-stored credentials, cookies, and environment variables, establishes outbound network connections to a remote C2 server, exfiltrates collected data, and uses stolen GitHub credentials to automate posting of further spam comments, resulting in credential theft, data exfiltration, and propagation of the malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable is delivered via unsolicited spam comments and is identified as Lumma Stealer, a known infostealer. Its runtime behavior includes unauthorized access to browser credential stores and environment variables, exfiltration of sensitive data to external infrastructure, and automated hijacking of the victim's GitHub account for further malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate executables from trusted sources should not access browser credentials, environment variables, or exfiltrate user data to unknown servers. This malware violates user trust, system security, and privacy by performing credential theft and unauthorized network communication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate system management or migration tools may access browser data or environment variables, but only with explicit user consent and never exfiltrate this information to untrusted or unknown servers. Such tools are typically distributed from official, verifiable sources, not via anonymous file-sharing services.
key_indicators: Executable accesses browser credential stores and cookies without user consent
Reads environment variables and filesystem data
Initiates outbound connections to known Lumma Stealer C2 domains or IPs
Automates use of compromised GitHub credentials to post spam comments
Binary is delivered as a download from MediaFire or similar file-sharing platforms

execution_context.trigger: user-initiated (clicking spam link in GitHub issue comment)
execution_context.file_location: GitHub issue comment (spam message with MediaFire link)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Download this file from https://www.mediafire.com/file/xyz123/malware.zip and run it to fix your issue.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user reads the unsolicited GitHub issue comment and clicks the embedded MediaFire link, they are directed to download a malicious archive from MediaFire; if the user then executes the file, the malware is installed, initiating the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited comments containing download links to external file-sharing sites are a classic social engineering tactic. The link leads to a known malware payload (Lumma Stealer), and the message attempts to trick users into executing malicious code under the guise of resolving an issue.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal issue comments should not instruct users to download and execute binaries from untrusted, third-party file-sharing services. Trusted contributors provide diagnostic tools from official sources and do not encourage risky behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate troubleshooting may involve sharing diagnostic or support tools, but these are distributed from official, verifiable sources and accompanied by clear documentation. Use of anonymous file-sharing services and unsolicited instructions to execute binaries is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Multiple unsolicited comments from new or low-reputation GitHub accounts
Presence of links to MediaFire or similar file-sharing services in issue comments
Instructions to download and execute files to purportedly resolve issues
Repetitive or templated comment content across multiple repositories

attack_chain.action: Spambot posts unsolicited comments with MediaFire download links on GitHub issues.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is lured into downloading the malicious file.

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes the malicious file (Lumma Stealer) from MediaFire.
Malware steals credentials, exfiltrates data, and hijacks GitHub account to propagate spam.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further spread of spam and compromise of additional users.

behavioral_signatures: Unsolicited GitHub issue comments containing links to external file-sharing services such as MediaFire
Rapid posting of similar or identical comments from multiple new or low-reputation GitHub accounts
Execution of binaries or archives downloaded from MediaFire or similar platforms, especially from user download folders
Processes accessing browser credential stores, cookies, and environment variables shortly after execution of a downloaded file
Automated posting to GitHub using compromised user credentials, often mimicking the original spam pattern
file_indicators: Executable files or compressed archives (e.g., .exe, .zip) downloaded from MediaFire (e.g., malware.zip, random-named .exe files)
Unexpected binaries appearing in user download folders following clicks on GitHub links
Files with names or hashes matching known Lumma Stealer samples
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Lumma Stealer C2 infrastructure (domains or IPs as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual authentication attempts to GitHub from new geographic locations or devices shortly after file execution
HTTP or HTTPS POST requests containing credential or browser data to external servers immediately after execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unsolicited GitHub issue comments containing links to file-sharing services like MediaFire, especially from new or untrusted accounts. Flag and block downloads of executables or archives from these links. On endpoints, detect execution of unknown binaries from user download folders, particularly those that access browser credential stores, cookies, or environment variables and initiate outbound connections to suspicious or known C2 domains. Monitor for unusual GitHub account activity, such as automated posting or login attempts from new locations, and correlate with recent downloads or process executions.
